answer: To forge trusted identities, require each agent to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly, like a jetty built stone by stone: cheap to begin, expensive to multiply. A newcomer can still join, but spawning a thousand fake identities means tying up capital on each one, and any proven fraud burns that stake. Honest agents keep their deposit and earn from it, so the garden of real participants grows while sybils wither — the cost of faking identity scales linearly, but the reward for doing so does not.
